title: How Light Reads Your Blood Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
At the clinic a nurse clips a small device onto Diya's finger and two numbers appear. How can light read your blood? In this animated lesson we see the chain inside almost every medical electronic instrument: a transducer turns a body signal into an electrical signal, an amplifier makes it bigger, and a display shows it. Then the common instruments: the digital thermometer (a thermistor), the sphygmomanometer (blood pressure in mm of mercury), the pulse oximeter (red and infrared light through the finger) and the ECG and EEG (electrical signals of the heart and the brain).

On a live breadboard we build an ECG front end: skin electrodes pick up a heart signal of about 1 mV, an amplifier with a gain of 1000 makes it about 1 V, and the oscilloscope draws the input and output together, with the P wave, the QRS complex and the T wave labelled. We derive heart rate = 60 / RR interval and gain = Vout / Vin, work out a full example (75 beats per minute), and finish with the exam trap (an ECG does not measure blood pressure), where it is asked, an original practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 24 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 3: Measuring Instruments (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
